explanation: There is a Tarski monster (every nontrivial proper subgroup has prime order p) with a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology. This is Klyachko–Olshanskii–Osin Theorem 1.4: topologizable Tarski Monsters exist for every sufficiently large odd exponent n. In KOO, Tarski Monsters are infinite simple groups with all proper subgroups finite cyclic, so taking n a large prime gives the Lean definition. The statement is correct and solved.
